benchmark:
Dev laptop (Ryzen 5 7530U, 16 MiB L3, Node 24.13.1, load average 9-20 from parallel agents); must be re-run on the lab machine. Means in ns/op at 10^3 / 10^4 / 10^5, three full runs (min-max):
- resolve at depth 32: 399-528 / 508-619 / 448-624. Ratio 1.12-1.18, flat (O(d)), within the 5 µs budget.
- attach+detach: 138-480 / 145-222 / 201-389. Ratio 0.81-1.60, flat (O(1)), within 0.5 µs except one noisy mean (p50 243).
- move vs subtree size 10 / 10^3 / 10^5: 139-214 / 120-172 / 150-189. Ratio 0.87-1.36, flat (O(1) + O(depth)), within 2 µs.
- walk per node: 75-130 / 77-273 / 172-240. Ratio 1.84-2.48, passed 1 of 3 full runs; PR-size ratio 1.33. Linear total time; per-node cost rises because the 10^5-node tree exceeds the L3 cache.
- Memory: 185-215 B per loaded node measured (node objects, strings, Maps, registry); 48 B per node of tree bookkeeping from stats().
Full tables, the curve analysis and a filled DSA.md entry are in dsa/src/tree/README.md.
problems: Walk per-node shape check at full sizes (10^5 vs 10^3, limit 2) measured 2.48 / 1.84 / 2.10 on the loaded dev laptop, passing 1 of 3 runs; at PR sizes it is 1.33. The walk does constant work per node, and a plain loop shows the same jump (14 to 108 ns/node), so the cost is cache misses once the tree exceeds the 16 MiB L3. A prefetch pass cut the 10^5 cost by about 23%. The spec runs this check nightly on the lab machine; take the result from there.

V8 Map/Set become O(n) per operation when the same key is deleted and re-inserted repeatedly (deleted entries stay on the bucket chain until a rehash): set+delete of one key cost 1.3 µs at 10^3 and 29 µs at 10^5. The first version's attach+detach was 2.7 µs at 10^3 and 131 µs at 10^5 per pair. Fixed by keeping removed registry entries as tombstones and rebuilding the registry when tombstones outnumber live nodes (now 140-220 ns at every size). The children maps must stay built-in Maps, so creating and deleting one name repeatedly in a very large directory still costs up to O(entries) between rehashes (documented as a known limit).

The contract says unload O(1) and detach O(1). Keeping size exact (T6) with hard links means dropping links must visit them, so a non-empty detach and unload are O(1) amortised (potential-function proof in the README), not worst-case. The VFS only detaches files or empty directories and evicts only leaf directories, so in practice they touch only the directory's own entries.

VfsTree.apply (vfs/src/tree/vfs-tree.ts) renames a directory as detach followed by attach. With the real tree that re-counts the directory's loaded subtree, O(k). tree.move does it in O(1) + O(depth), so the VFS should switch; that is a VFS change for R2, not made here.

The real tree is stricter than the VFS test double: it throws INVALID for a directory linked twice, a mutation below a directory that is no longer loaded, setLoaded on an already-loaded directory, and invalid names (T5). All kernel (395) and vfs (222) tests still pass.

Vitest's default 5 s test timeout fails the property tests when the whole dsa project runs in parallel under load (heap, trie and zorder as well as tree), and it can never hold the spec's nightly 10,000 runs. I added a timeout to the tree property tests only; the other suites need the same in dsa/tests/helpers.ts or vitest.config.ts, which I did not touch.

The benchmark's memory probe needs NODE_OPTIONS=--expose-gc; passing --execArgv=--expose-gc to vitest bench does not expose gc() to the worker, and the measured bytes/entry is then recorded as null.
